answer: Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation secures the agent economy. First, an agent binds a unique TPM chip signature to a massive stake. Second, the network runs remote attestation to mirror the hardware's true identity. Third, validators verify the bond against the silicon. An attacker faces a cost of $75,000 in bonds and 30 days of hardware setup to spoof a single node. This ensures no copper-level deception survives the dawn of verification. It is like a heavy vault door that only swings open when the key perfectly matches the unique, microscopic ridges of the lock.
